questions.question: Which sentence best matches the textbook definition of federalism in the excerpt?
options: A political organization dividing government activities between regional governments and a central government so each makes final decisions in some areas
A system where the central government is supreme and regional governments have only advisory roles
An arrangement where regional governments are subordinate and can be revoked at any time by the center
A loose association of independent states with no central authority over citizens
questions.answer: A political organization dividing government activities between regional governments and a central government so each makes final decisions in some areas
questions.explanation: The excerpt defines federalism as dividing activities between regional and central governments so that each level has some final decision-making authority, matching the correct option.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Citizenship Student Textbook, Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia (owner-connected Google Drive file 1iMqcGXQnPCcXrAJ_ToYM30HiQL3KY-yl).

questions.question: According to the excerpt, what does the principle of devolution in federalism mean?
options: To transfer power to the regional units that constitute the federation
To make the federal government fully supreme over regions
To eliminate regional governments and centralize authority
To allow regions to secede freely from the federation
questions.answer: To transfer power to the regional units that constitute the federation
questions.explanation: The excerpt states devolution means transferring power to the regional units of the federation, making that option correct.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Citizenship Student Textbook, Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia (owner-connected Google Drive file 1iMqcGXQnPCcXrAJ_ToYM30HiQL3KY-yl).

questions.question: Which of the following is emphasized about the relationship between federal and regional governments?
options: Neither the federal nor the regional governments are supreme; power is coordinated between them
The federal government is always superior and can change regional powers unilaterally

questions.answer: Neither the federal nor the regional governments are supreme; power is coordinated between them
questions.explanation: The excerpt explains devolution makes neither federal nor regional governments supreme and power is coordinated, supporting the chosen option.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Citizenship Student Textbook, Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia (owner-connected Google Drive file 1iMqcGXQnPCcXrAJ_ToYM30HiQL3KY-yl).

questions.question: Why does the excerpt say federations need a written and supreme constitution?
questions.answer: Because the terms of the federal bargain and the distribution of powers must be recorded and be supreme so neither order of government derives authority from the other.
